scripts.title: When the guest returns, the commission does too
scripts.cold_viewer_context: A small inn takes a booking through a booking site and pays it a commission; a year later the same guest books the same room through the same booking site.
scripts.hook_line: what did that second stay actually cost her,
scripts.payoff_line: she pays the site the same commission she paid the first time.
scripts.standalone_payoff: The second booking costs the inn a second commission the same size as the first, charged on a guest the inn already had.
scripts.closing_line: I couldn't find anyone selling it who'd done that arithmetic.
scripts.last_line: I couldn't find anyone selling it who'd done that arithmetic.
scripts.spoken_copy: what did that second stay actually cost her, and who gets paid to stop it? And she pays the site the same commission she paid the first time. For a guest she already knows by name. I couldn't find anyone selling it who'd done that arithmetic.
scripts.episode_extension: The four modeled inputs that price the work, and the monthly ceiling they produce for an illustrative inn.
scripts.pinned_comment:
Full episode: [EPISODE_URL]

The arithmetic this Short stops short of: the inn's four modeled inputs, the reported commission band, and the ceiling that caps what an outside operator could charge for the work. Commission mechanics are from Booking.com's own partner help, which says commission is a set percentage of the whole booking, charged at checkout.
description: A small inn takes a booking through a booking site, pays commission, and then the same guest books the same way again.
Commission is charged per booking, so the second stay costs the inn what the first one did, on a guest it already had. Booking.com's own partner help describes that mechanic.
Nobody selling a fix for it has published the arithmetic. EP009 runs it on an illustrative 20-room inn.
